items.title: The Scout listens to Inez

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Inez, have you eaten anything since this morning? You've hardly left that doorway all shift.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I can't stop, Milena. Another letter came from the Bureau today, and I'm three payments behind now.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Three behind? Oh, love, you never said it had got that bad.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I didn't want anyone to know. Whatever I pay, they add more on, and now their man comes asking for me here.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Here, in front of the whole terrace? No wonder you can't keep still.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Some days I'd give anything to sit down for five minutes and not think about any of it.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: You wouldn't sit for long, though. You'd be up the moment the guard on the Office door looked this way.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: What do you mean by that?

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Only that you've looked across that square more often today than you've looked at your own tables.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Has Arthur said something to you?

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: He's never said a word to me. You've just told me his name yourself, love.
beats.revealAfter: He's never said a word to me.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Oh, Milena. Yes, it's Arthur, and nobody knows, and nobody can know.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: I'd never tell a soul, you know that. But why must it be such a secret?

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: If the Office hears of it, he'll lose his post, and I'll lose him. I can't bear to lose anything else.

beats.speaker: milena
beats.line: Then it stays between us. Just keep your eyes on your tables, or someone else will see what I saw.

beats.speaker: scout
beats.line: She's deep in debt to the Bureau and can't keep up. And she's seeing Arthur, the guard on the Office door.

notes: Sky's note 1: Milena has no debt of her own now, so nothing to compete with. She asks ("Three behind?", "in front of the whole terrace?") and is sorry for her, and each answer makes Inez's trouble worse: three payments behind, more added whatever she pays, their man asking for her at work.

Same facts, same order of discovery: the Bureau and being behind; the guard; she gives his name away herself; if the Office hears, it costs them both. Her nerves show in the questions and in giving way, never in a word for fear.
Milena's reveal keeps its beat ("He's never said a word to me." first, the rest 0.9 s later).
The Scout's last line reports only what was heard, in the words of the two cards (Debt, Secret). 16 lines: at the limit.

items.title: The Fixer helps Inez, first visit

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Forgive me for stopping you between tables, Miss Nikolaou. I've brought you money, half of what you owe the Bureau.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You've brought me what?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Half of what you owe, and it's yours. Give it to them, and you'll be caught up at last.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I don't know you. How do you know what I owe?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: People talk in a square like this one. I listen, and I don't repeat what I hear.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Did anyone see you give it to me?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nobody was watching. From the terrace, I'm a customer asking you the way.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Nobody hands a stranger money for nothing. What is it you want from me?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nothing today. One day soon I may ask you a small favour, and it won't hurt anybody.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Then thank you, truly. But I can't promise you anything for it, not yet.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I haven't asked you to. Pay what you can with it, and I'll come back with the rest.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You'd give me all of it? Nobody does that for a stranger.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Then I'll be the first. Go back to your tables, Miss Nikolaou, before anyone wonders who I am.

notes: Sky's note 2: the Fixer gives the money to Inez; she clears the loan with it. Nobody goes to the Bureau, and nothing is stamped or filed. "Half" is exact: a fearful Inez takes two visits at $20,000 of the $40,000 (rulebook worse-help-usd), and this scene plays only on the first of them.
No envelope or other prop named: the game pays away from the shot (the scene checks' rule).
Three questions in three turns, each answered before the next: How do you know? Did anyone see? What do you want? Still says, in these words, that the Fixer will come back with the rest.

items.title: The Fixer helps Inez, second visit

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I said I'd come back, Miss Nikolaou, and I've brought the rest. With it you can clear the whole loan.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Please, not so loud. People can hear you from the terrace.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Forgive me. I forget how far a voice carries out here.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I've owed the Bureau for years. I keep waiting to feel lighter, and I don't, not yet.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Give it a day or two. You carried it longer than most people could have.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You said you'd bring the rest, and you did. So what is it you want from me?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: A few minutes of someone's time. When I telephone the café, I'd like you to call Arthur over from his door.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: So you know about us. How long have you known?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Long enough to know it's nobody's business but yours. Nobody will hear it from me.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: What happens to him, if I call him over?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nothing, if this goes the way it should. He'll be at your side, and he'll never see us.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: He won't leave that door for nothing. I'll tell him I've something to say that can't go down a telephone.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Then tell him that. You know him better than anyone does.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: You kept your word to me, so I'll keep mine.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I watch that square all day anyway. If I see trouble coming for you, I'll find a way to warn you.

notes: Sky agreed today's version on 2026-11-01; this reopens it.
Sky's note 2: the first line was "That's the rest paid. You owe the Bureau nothing"; now the Fixer brings her the rest and she can clear the loan with it.

Her offer to warn now says "trouble coming for you" where the first draft said "before you telephone": a helped Inez warns the cell 10 s early in the fight at the car (GDD §07 safe), which is after the call, not before it.
Kept: the ask, her fright at "Arthur", what happens to him, her reason for getting him off the door (said aloud, which the call relies on).

items.title: The Fixer presses Inez

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: If you're from the Bureau, I know I'm behind. I'll have something for you by the end of the week.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I'm not from the Bureau, Miss Nikolaou. I've come about you and Arthur, on the Office door.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: How do you know about that?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: It doesn't matter how. What matters is that the Office could hear of it before the day is out.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Please don't. Whatever it is you want, I'll do it.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Hear it first, Miss Nikolaou, and take a breath. Nobody's in a hurry here.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Then say it quickly. I've tables waiting, and they're already looking this way.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: When I telephone the café, call Arthur over from his door. That's all I'll ask of you.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: He'd come if I asked him. He trusts me.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I know he does. That's why it has to be you.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: And if I won't do it?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Then the Office hears about the two of you, and I'd be sorry for it. I'd rather it never came to that.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Then I'll do it. Now go, please, before anyone sees me talking to you.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Thank you. See to your tables, Miss Nikolaou, and keep this between the two of us.

notes: New in this draft. No money changes hands (Pressure is $0). Her first line takes a stranger for the Bureau's man: a fearful woman behind on her payments, and it sets up who the Fixer isn't before the Fixer says why they've come.
The threat is plain by the end and never raised: warm manner, steel under it. She gives way too fast and never says she's scared.
"Keep this between the two of us" is the Fixer's "not a word to Arthur"; the call after Pressure repeats it. She will know the Fixer's face (the card says so); nobody says it aloud.

items.title: The Fixer pays Lukac

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: You're Lukac, the Councillor's driver? You don't know me, and it's better for both of us if it stays that way.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: Then say what you want quickly. I'm on the Councillor's time, not mine.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I hear your wages are late again, and that every hour you wait out here costs you.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: Who've you been talking to?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nobody who'll mention it again. I've work for a driver, and I pay well, and I pay now.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: What sort of work?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: One drive with the Councillor, today. An easy one.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: I've been promised easy drives before. Tell me exactly where it goes.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: When the chime goes, he'll come out and get in as he always does. But you don't take him home.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: Then where do I take him?

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Round to the service bay at the back of the Office. You pull in there, and you wait.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: The east yard. I'll give you a couple of minutes there, and then I drive on.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: That's fair. We'll be at the bay when you pull in.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: And don't tell me who 'we' are. What I don't know, nobody can ask me about later.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: I wish everyone I dealt with had your sense, Lukac. The money's yours.

beats.speaker: driver
beats.line: It's been a lean month, so I'll take it. Anyone hanging about that bay, I'll send off, and I won't be looking.

notes: Sky agreed today's version on 2026-11-02; this reopens it.

Sky's note 3: it no longer opens on "So it's paid". The Fixer comes as a stranger who'd rather stay one, says what she knows (his wages are late, waiting costs him: what the Scout's Listen overheard), offers work paid on the spot, then the job. His lean month and his taking the money come last, as his reaction.

The amount isn't spoken: the Pay card shows it, and it moves ($70,000 on the reference; $20,000 less if a Watch found him friendly; rulebook turn.pay). Help on Lukac ($40,000) has no scene of its own yet; it plays the act's street lines.

Same job, same terms: at the chime he gets in, not home but the service bay in the east yard, a couple of minutes, then Lukac drives on; can send off anyone watching the bay; won't look; doesn't want to know who "we" are, and says why.

items.title: The call, after Help

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: It's time, Miss Nikolaou. Call Arthur across now, the way we said, and you'll do fine.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Now, with the terrace this full? Yes, all right, I'll do it.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: He trusts me, you know. Promise me again that nothing happens to him.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: Nothing, if this goes the way it should. You have my word.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Arthur, it's me. How's your shift going, love?

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Long and quiet. Nobody's been to the door all day, so it's good to hear you.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Come across to me for a bit. I've something to tell you, and it can't go down a telephone.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: I've this door till the shift ends. For you, it can wait a while.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Walk, love, don't run. I'd like to keep you a while.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Keep me as long as you like.

notes: Sky agreed today's version on 2026-11-01 (plain pass 2026-11-02); this reopens it. No mention of the Bureau or the money, so Sky's note 2 didn't touch it; it's rewritten to the full-sentence rules so the seven read as one piece.
New: two lines where she asks the Fixer again that Arthur comes to no harm, and gets the same answer as on the second visit. It's the tenderness the scene is for: she loves him, and she's using it.
Kept: the 1.2 s pause before she speaks to him, the lean on "you", the 1.5 s hold on her face at the end, and her reason ("can't go down a telephone").

items.title: The call, after Pressure

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: It's time, Miss Nikolaou. Call Arthur over now.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: Yes. I said I would, and I will.

beats.speaker: fixer
beats.line: You're doing well. Remember, not a word about me to him.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I heard you the first time.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: It's me, love. How long is it till your shift ends?

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Too long, and you sound worn out. What is it, Inez?

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: I've something to tell you, and it can't go down a telephone.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: Can it wait till I'm off? I've this door till then.

beats.speaker: waitress
beats.line: It can't wait, love. Please, come now.

beats.speaker: guard
beats.line: It's only a door. All right, I'm coming over.

street.speaker: waitress
street.line: Someone knows about us, love. They looked suspicious.

street.speaker: guard
street.line: Then my door's standing empty. Stay here, Inez.

notes: Sky agreed today's version on 2026-11-01 (plain pass 2026-11-02); this reopens it. No Bureau or money in it; rewritten to the full-sentence rules.
New: "I heard you the first time." She has no warmth left for the Fixer, and with Arthur she sounds ordinary. Same reason, same "Can it wait?", same ending: he's coming.

A 1.2 s pause before she speaks to him, as in the call after Help, so the cut between the two calls reads the same. The two street bubbles when he reaches her ("Someone knows about us") are unchanged: bubbles keep the 12-word limit.
